passages.text: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
passages.sermon:
Ahithophel was a trusted advisor.
Absalom was the son of King David.
Ahithophel spoke to Absalom.
He said, “Let me choose twelve thousand men.
I will get up tonight.
I will chase after David.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם אֶבְחֲרָ֣ה נָּ֗א שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֙לֶף֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְאָק֛וּמָה וְאֶרְדְּפָ֥ה אַחֲרֵי־ דָוִ֖ד הַלָּֽיְלָה׃

passages.text: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
passages.sermon:
Ahithophel was a trusted advisor.
People respected his advice like the word of God.
Both David and Absalom valued his counsel.
Ahithophel spoke to Absalom about David.
He said, “I will go to David.
David will be tired and weak.
I will frighten him.
All the people with David will run away.
I will strike down only the king.
I will bring all the people back to you, Absalom.
You want only one man, David.
After this, all the people will be at peace.”
passages.original: וְאָב֣וֹא עָלָ֗יו וְה֤וּא יָגֵ֙עַ֙ וּרְפֵ֣ה יָדַ֔יִם וְהַֽחֲרַדְתִּ֣י אֹת֔וֹ וְנָ֖ס כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֑וֹ וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י אֶת־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃ וְאָשִׁ֥יבָה כָל־ הָעָ֖ם אֵלֶ֑יךָ כְּשׁ֣וּב הַכֹּ֔ל הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
The elders of Israel were the leaders of the people.
Ahithophel gave a proposal to Absalom and the elders.
Absalom liked the proposal.
All the elders of Israel also liked the proposal.
passages.original: וַיִּישַׁ֥ר הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ זִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

passages.text: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom spoke to his advisors.
He said, "Call Hushai the Archite."
He wanted Hushai to come to them.
Absalom said, "Let us hear what Hushai will say."
He wanted to know Hushai's advice.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם קְרָ֣א נָ֔א גַּ֖ם לְחוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֑י וְנִשְׁמְעָ֥ה מַה־ בְּפִ֖יו גַּם־ הֽוּא׃

passages.text: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
passages.sermon:
Hushai was a trusted advisor.
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom wanted advice about a proposal.
Hushai came to Absalom.
Absalom spoke to Hushai.
Absalom said, “Ahithophel has given this advice.”
Absalom asked, “Should we do what he said?”
Absalom also asked, “If not, what do you say?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣א חוּשַׁי֮ אֶל־ אַבְשָׁלוֹם֒ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כַּדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲחִיתֹ֔פֶל הֲנַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־ דְּבָר֑וֹ אִם־ אַ֖יִן אַתָּ֥ה דַבֵּֽר׃ס

passages.text: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
passages.sermon: Hushai spoke to Absalom.\r\nHushai said, "Ahithophel gave advice this time."\r\nThis advice is not good.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חוּשַׁ֖י אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא־ טוֹבָ֧ה הָעֵצָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־ יָעַ֥ץ אֲחִיתֹ֖פֶל בַּפַּ֥עַם הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
passages.sermon:
Hushai spoke to Absalom.
He said, “You know your father David.
You know his men.
They are mighty men.
They are fierce in spirit.
They are like a wild bear robbed of her cubs in the field.
Your father is a man of war.
He will not stay with the troops at night.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אַתָּ֣ה יָ֠דַעְתָּ אֶת־ אָבִ֨יךָ וְאֶת־ אֲנָשָׁ֜יו כִּ֧י גִבֹּרִ֣ים הֵ֗מָּה וּמָרֵ֥י נֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ הֵ֔מָּה כְּדֹ֥ב שַׁכּ֖וּל בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְאָבִ֙יךָ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יָלִ֖ין אֶת־ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
passages.sermon:
David is your father.
David is a man of war.
David is not with the main troops.
Right now, David is hiding.
He may be in a cave.
He may be in another place.
If your men attack first, some of your men may fall.
Someone will hear about it.
That person will say, “There has been a defeat among the people who follow Absalom.”
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה עַתָּ֤ה הֽוּא־ נֶחְבָּא֙ בְּאַחַ֣ת הַפְּחָתִ֔ים א֖וֹ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַמְּקוֹמֹ֑ת וְהָיָ֗ה כִּנְפֹ֤ל בָּהֶם֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה וְשָׁמַ֤ע הַשֹּׁמֵ֙עַ֙ וְאָמַ֔ר הָֽיְתָה֙ מַגֵּפָ֔ה בָּעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֹֽם׃

passages.text: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
passages.sermon:
A valiant soldier may have a heart as brave as a lion.
Even this brave soldier will lose courage.
He will melt with fear.
All Israel knows your father is a mighty man.
All Israel knows your father has valiant men with him.
passages.original: וְה֣וּא גַם־ בֶּן־ חַ֗יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִבּ֛וֹ כְּלֵ֥ב הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הִמֵּ֣ס יִמָּ֑ס כִּֽי־ יֹדֵ֤עַ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּי־ גִבּ֣וֹר אָבִ֔יךָ וּבְנֵי־ חַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
passages.sermon:
Hushai the Archite spoke to Absalom.
Hushai gave advice about attacking David.
Hushai said, “Gather all Israel to you.
Gather people from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
The people will be as many as the sand by the sea.
You, Absalom, must lead them into battle.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י יָעַ֗צְתִּי הֵ֠אָסֹף יֵאָסֵ֨ף עָלֶ֤יךָ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִדָּן֙ וְעַד־ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר־ עַל־ הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב וּפָנֶ֥יךָ הֹלְכִ֖ים בַּקְרָֽב׃

passages.text: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
passages.sermon:
David is the king of Israel.
David has men with him.
We will go to David.
We will find him at one of the places where he is.
We will attack him there.
We will come down on him like dew falls on the ground.
None of his men will remain.
Not even one man with him will be left.
passages.original: וּבָ֣אנוּ אֵלָ֗יו בְּאַחַת הַמְּקוֹמֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם וְנַ֣חְנוּ עָלָ֔יו כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִפֹּ֥ל הַטַּ֖ל עַל־ הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ נ֥וֹתַר בּ֛וֹ וּבְכָל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ גַּם־ אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found.”
passages.sermon:
If David retreats to a city, all Israel will act together.
All Israel will bring ropes to that city.
We will drag the city down to the valley.
We will continue until not even a pebble is left there.
passages.original: וְאִם־ אֶל־ עִיר֙ יֵֽאָסֵ֔ף וְהִשִּׂ֧יאוּ כָֽל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־ הָעִ֥יר הַהִ֖יא חֲבָלִ֑ים וְסָחַ֤בְנוּ אֹתוֹ֙ עַד־ הַנַּ֔חַל עַ֛ד אֲשֶֽׁר־ לֹא־ נִמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם גַּם־ צְרֽוֹר׃פ

passages.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
All the men of Israel were with Absalom.
Absalom and all the men of Israel spoke together.
They said that Hushai the Archite gave better advice than Ahithophel.
The LORD had decided to stop the good advice of Ahithophel.
The LORD did this to bring disaster on Absalom.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ וְכָל־ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל טוֹבָ֗ה עֲצַת֙ חוּשַׁ֣י הָאַרְכִּ֔י מֵעֲצַ֖ת אֲחִיתֹ֑פֶל וַיהוָ֣ה צִוָּ֗ה לְהָפֵ֞ר אֶת־ עֲצַ֤ת אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה לְבַעֲב֗וּר הָבִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶת־ הָרָעָֽה׃ס

passages.text: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
passages.sermon:
Hushai was a counselor and a friend of King David.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Hushai spoke to Zadok and Abiathar.
Hushai said, “Ahithophel gave this advice to Absalom and the elders of Israel.
I gave different advice.
This is what Ahithophel advised.
This is what I advised.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חוּשַׁ֗י אֶל־ צָד֤וֹק וְאֶל־ אֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים כָּזֹ֣את וְכָזֹ֗את יָעַ֤ץ אֲחִיתֹ֙פֶל֙ אֶת־ אַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָזֹ֥את וְכָזֹ֖את יָעַ֥צְתִּי אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Hushai was a friend and supporter of King David.
Hushai spoke to Zadok and Abiathar.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Hushai said, “Send a message quickly to David.”
He said, “Tell David this.”
“Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness.”
“Cross over the river tonight.”
“If you do not cross, the king will be in danger.”
“All the people with the king will also be in danger.”
“They could all be destroyed.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה שִׁלְח֣וּ מְהֵרָה֩ וְהַגִּ֨ידוּ לְדָוִ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר אַל־ תָּ֤לֶן הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ בְּעַֽרְב֣וֹת הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְגַ֖ם עָב֣וֹר תַּעֲב֑וֹר פֶּ֚ן יְבֻלַּ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
passages.sermon:
Jonathan and Ahimaaz were at En-rogel.
They did not go into the city.
They did not want to be seen.
A servant girl came to them at En-rogel.
She gave them information.
Jonathan and Ahimaaz took the message.
They went to tell King David.
passages.original: וִיהוֹנָתָ֨ן וַאֲחִימַ֜עַץ עֹמְדִ֣ים בְּעֵין־ רֹגֵ֗ל וְהָלְכָ֤ה הַשִּׁפְחָה֙ וְהִגִּ֣ידָה לָהֶ֔ם וְהֵם֙ יֵֽלְכ֔וּ וְהִגִּ֖ידוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֛וּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת לָב֥וֹא הָעִֽירָה׃

passages.text: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
passages.sermon:
A young man saw Jonathan and Ahimaaz.
He told Absalom about them.
Jonathan and Ahimaaz left quickly.
They went to the house of a man in Bahurim.
This man had a well in his courtyard.
Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed down into the well.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא אֹתָם֙ נַ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְשָׁלֹ֑ם וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ שְׁנֵיהֶ֨ם מְהֵרָ֜ה וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ׀ אֶל־ בֵּֽית־ אִ֣ישׁ בְּבַחוּרִ֗ים וְל֥וֹ בְאֵ֛ר בַּחֲצֵר֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥רְדוּ שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Then the man’s wife took a covering and spread it over the mouth of the well, scattering grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
passages.sermon:
A man lived in Bahurim.
His wife acted to hide Jonathan and Ahimaaz.
She took a covering.
She spread the covering over the mouth of the well.
She scattered grain on top of the covering.
No one knew that Jonathan and Ahimaaz were in the well.
passages.original: וַתִּקַּ֣ח הָאִשָּׁ֗ה וַתִּפְרֹ֤שׂ אֶת־ הַמָּסָךְ֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַתִּשְׁטַ֥ח עָלָ֖יו הָֽרִפ֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א נוֹדַ֖ע דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” “They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom’s servants came to a house.
A woman lived in that house.
The servants spoke to the woman.
They asked her a question.
They said, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?”
Ahimaaz and Jonathan were messengers loyal to David.
The woman answered the servants.
She said, “They have crossed over the brook.”
The servants searched for Ahimaaz and Jonathan.
They did not find them.
The servants returned to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ עַבְדֵי֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶֽל־ הָאִשָּׁ֜ה הַבַּ֗יְתָה וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֗ה אֲחִימַ֙עַץ֙ וִיה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה עָבְר֖וּ מִיכַ֣ל הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֔אוּ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
passages.sermon:
Ahimaaz and Jonathan were messengers loyal to King David.
Absalom’s men searched for them but did not find them.
After Absalom’s men left, Ahimaaz and Jonathan came up from the well.
They went to King David.
They spoke to David.
They said, “Get up and cross the river quickly.”
They said, “Ahithophel has given advice against you.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ אַחֲרֵ֣י לֶכְתָּ֗ם וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ מֵֽהַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־ דָּוִ֗ד ק֣וּמוּ וְעִבְר֤וּ מְהֵרָה֙ אֶת־ הַמַּ֔יִם כִּי־ כָ֛כָה יָעַ֥ץ עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם אֲחִיתֹֽפֶל׃

passages.text: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David had many people with him.
David and all the people got up.
They crossed the Jordan River together.
They kept crossing until morning light.
By daybreak, everyone had crossed the Jordan.
No one was left behind.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־ הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן עַד־ א֣וֹר הַבֹּ֗קֶר עַד־ אַחַד֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ עָבַ֖ר אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
passages.sermon:
Ahithophel was a counselor.
Ahithophel saw that no one followed his advice.
He saddled his donkey.
He left and went to his house in his hometown.
He put his affairs in order.
He hanged himself.
He died.
People buried him in his father’s tomb.
passages.original: וַאֲחִיתֹ֣פֶל רָאָ֗ה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נֶעֶשְׂתָה֮ עֲצָתוֹ֒ וַיַּחֲבֹ֣שׁ אֶֽת־ הַחֲמ֗וֹר וַיָּ֜קָם וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ אֶל־ עִיר֔וֹ וַיְצַ֥ו אֶל־ בֵּית֖וֹ וַיֵּחָנַ֑ק וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּקֶ֥בֶר אָבִֽיו׃ס

passages.text: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David went to Mahanaim.
Absalom was David’s son and his enemy.
Absalom crossed the Jordan River.
All the men of Israel went with Absalom.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֖ד בָּ֣א מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֗ם עָבַר֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן ה֕וּא וְכָל־ אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of King David.
Absalom led a rebellion against his father David.
Absalom appointed Amasa as commander of the army.
Amasa replaced Joab as commander.
Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra.
Ithra was an Ishmaelite.
Ithra married Abigail.
Abigail was the daughter of Nahash.
Abigail was the sister of Zeruiah.
Zeruiah was the mother of Joab.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ עֲמָשָׂ֗א שָׂ֧ם אַבְשָׁלֹ֛ם תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָ֖ב עַל־ הַצָּבָ֑א וַעֲמָשָׂ֣א בֶן־ אִ֗ישׁ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יִתְרָ֣א הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־ בָּא֙ אֶל־ אֲבִיגַ֣ל בַּת־ נָחָ֔שׁ אֲח֥וֹת צְרוּיָ֖ה אֵ֥ם יוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
passages.sermon:
Absalom was the son of David.
Absalom led the Israelites.
Absalom and the Israelites camped together.
They camped in the land of Gilead.
passages.original: וַיִּ֤חַן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאַבְשָׁלֹ֔ם אֶ֖רֶץ הַגִּלְעָֽד׃ס

passages.text: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David came to Mahanaim.
Shobi met David.
Shobi was the son of Nahash.
Shobi was from Rabbah of the Ammonites.
Machir also met David.
Machir was the son of Ammiel.
Machir was from Lo-debar.
Barzillai also met David.
Barzillai was a Gileadite.
Barzillai was from Rogelim.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כְּב֥וֹא דָוִ֖ד מַחֲנָ֑יְמָה וְשֹׁבִ֨י בֶן־ נָחָ֜שׁ מֵרַבַּ֣ת בְּנֵֽי־ עַמּ֗וֹן וּמָכִ֤יר בֶּן־ עַמִּיאֵל֙ מִלֹּ֣א דְבָ֔ר וּבַרְזִלַּ֥י הַגִּלְעָדִ֖י מֵרֹגְלִֽים׃

passages.text: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
passages.sermon:
Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought supplies to David and his people.
They brought beds.
They brought basins.
They brought earthen vessels.
They brought wheat.
They brought barley.
They brought flour.
They brought roasted grain.
They brought beans.
They brought lentils.
They brought honey.
They brought curds.
They brought sheep.
They brought cheese from the herd.
They gave these things to David and to the people with him to eat.
The people were hungry.
The people were exhausted.
The people were thirsty in the wilderness.
passages.original: מִשְׁכָּ֤ב וְסַפּוֹת֙ וּכְלִ֣י יוֹצֵ֔ר וְחִטִּ֥ים וּשְׂעֹרִ֖ים וְקֶ֣מַח וְקָלִ֑י וּפ֥וֹל וַעֲדָשִׁ֖ים וְקָלִֽי׃ וּדְבַ֣שׁ וְחֶמְאָ֗ה וְצֹאן֙ וּשְׁפ֣וֹת בָּקָ֔ר הִגִּ֧ישׁוּ לְדָוִ֛ד וְלָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־ אִתּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכ֑וֹל כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ הָעָ֗ם רָעֵ֛ב וְעָיֵ֥ף וְצָמֵ֖א בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃
